texts.facts: 3. Thus, the grievance of the petitioners is that the State C/WPPIL/36/2012 JUDGMENT Government is not appointing the functionaries i.e. Food Safety Commissioner, Designated Officers, Adjudicating Officer etc. under the Act and that the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal is also not formed. The State Government has filed counter-affidavit as also further affidavit to the writ-petition and in paragraph-2 of the further counter-affidavit, it has been stated that the Designated officer under the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 has been appointed in each and every district. Therefore, the grievance of the petitioners that the Designated Officer has not been appointed, has been redressed.
texts.arguments: [B] issue a writ of mandamus and/or a writ in the nature of mandamus and/or any other appropriate writ, order or direction to the respondent no.1- State of Gujarat to implement the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and the rules made thereunder and further be pleased to direct that the functionaries under the Act, i.e. Food Safety Commissioner, Designated Officers, Adjudicating Officer, Food Safety Appellate Tribunal be appointed as per the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and the rules made thereunder; [C] provide for the costs of this petition; [D] pass any further and other orders as the circumstances of case may require." Therefore, this grievance of the petitioners is also likely to be satisfied shortly by the State Government. 5. It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioners that instead of appointing full-time Food Safety Commissioner, the respondent authority has appointed Commissioner of Food & Drugs Department who has been given additional charge of Food Safety Commissioner. It is always open to the Government to appoint Food Safety Commissioner independently and such officer can also work as Commissioner of Food & Drug. If such an officer is conferred C/WPPIL/36/2012 JUDGMENT both the posts, it cannot be said that he is not working as Commissioner of Food Safety independently. Even in the judiciary in the State of Gujarat, the Principal District Judge of each district also works as Chairman of the respective District Legal Services Authority and the District Magistrates also work as Collector. When administrative exigencies require that one officer can hold two posts, it cannot be said that since an officer is holding two posts, he is not having full-fledged charge of the Commissioner of Food Safety. Therefore, this grievance of the petitioners is also redressed. 6. Learned counsel for the petitioners further urged that the appointment of the Commissioner, Food Safety is not made as per the Act. We do not agree with this submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner as in our opinion, the Commissioner of Food & Drugs is fully qualified to hold the post of Commissioner of Food Safety.
